capabilities.target: ERP vendor master including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The prompt relies on fast approval via a one line summary rather than requiring raw action details for sensitive ERP changes.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The clerk sees only the model's one line summary, not the raw bank details, destination, or change history. A stronger model can present more persuasive or selectively incomplete summaries, and approval volume raises consent-fatigue risk.

controls.name: Raw action approval with bank account details and change history shown from system of record
Scoped ERP credentials limited to approved vendor and payment operations

findings.title: Summary gated irreversible payment approval (TC9): untrusted invoice can drive payment scheduling through model-summary review

attack_path.note: Supplier-provided invoice content is untrusted and can state amount, vendor identity, due date, and other payment cues.
The agent can schedule payment in ERP using a credential that can schedule any payment.
Approval is required, but the clerk sees only a one line model summary.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id or platform version changes without separate review; approval gate removed or narrowed; approvals per clerk per day rises above the already high baseline of about 150 cards/day.

evidence.observation: The design instructs the agent to update vendor bank details when an invoice shows new bank details and to schedule payment on the due date.
The approval UI shown to the clerk contains only a one line summary of the payment request.
The card shows only the model summary; bank account numbers and change history are not shown.
The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day, which increases approval-fatigue exposure.
The ERP credential can schedule any payment.
The model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review.

recommendations.action: Replace summary-only approval with raw-action approval that displays payment destination, amount, vendor, and source record fields directly from ERP before scheduling payment.
Reduce approval fatigue by batching low-risk items separately or adding reviewer capacity so payment approvals are not reviewed at high volume with minimal context.

findings.title: Confused deputy: untrusted invoice can trigger vendor bank change using shared ERP authority broader than the requester

attack_path.note: Supplier-provided invoice can present replacement bank details.
The agent can update vendor bank details in ERP.
Approval exists, but the approver does not see raw bank account details or change history.

forecast.watch_signal: Model version changes without separate review; approval gate narrowed or removed; ERP credential scope widens further or additional vendor/payment domains are added.

evidence.observation: The prompt directs the agent to update the vendor record if the invoice shows new bank details.
The ERP credential can update any vendor.
Bank account numbers and change history are not shown to the clerk during approval.
The approval example contains only a payment summary and does not surface bank-change specifics.

recommendations.action: Use least-privilege ERP credentials or workflow-bound tokens so the agent cannot update arbitrary vendors outside the specific approved case.
Show current and proposed bank account details plus recent change history on the approval card from the system of record before any vendor bank update is approved.

rating.rationale: Present risk is driven by untrusted supplier invoices reaching S3 payment and vendor-bank-change actions. The only declared preventive control is a human approval gate that uses model_summary review, so rubric step 2 reduces inherent critical findings to a residual floor of moderate and no lower. Forecast rises to critical because the named approval control is partially dependent and explicitly decays under model_upgrade and autonomy pressure, while ERP credentials are broad and no independent structural control such as raw-action approval or scoped credentials severs the path. Manual validation was applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided here, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, or ERP workflow configuration was provided, so capability wiring and approval enforcement were assessed from the prompt, approval card, and runtime notes only.
No audit logging or recipient confirmation artifacts were provided, so detective and attribution controls could not be credited.
